question.prompt: Rationalize the denominator: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{3}}=k(\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{3})\). What is the value of \(k\)? (Write your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.)

solutions.explanation: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{3}\): \(\frac{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{3}}{5-3}=\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{3})\), so \(k=\frac{1}{2}\).
solutions.title: Rationalize with the conjugate
